So a while back The Boss solicitated/inspired me to do a write up on loneliness but I haven't been in the mood for such a post in a while. So while I'm waiting for a free doctor to look at my eye injury, I'll put the properly functioning one to good use & do some mobile writing.

We've all experienced some form of loneliness at least once in our lives, usually not voluntarily, but sometimes so. Personally, I'm a social introvert, I adore socializing with others but I get drained and must eventually recharge my energies by being in my bubble with my wild wandering thoughts or by focusing on an idea that's bugging me and that I want to refine... sometimes I just smoke a joint & relax by watching a movie. As long as I get my space to myself for a bit after being Mr. Social.

This type of isolation was customary to me, and a must. Back then I was teaching trades full time which meants a lot of homework for lesson plans, attending 2 classes per semester at Uni and working a 2nd job part time to help a friend with her restaurant. So sometimes I just shut the world out & stayed in the basement for a day of whatever, it was my way of decompressing from all the pressure I was under. I had a full plate but I could manage it fine. I was feeling lonely after a while because I lacked the time to dedicate part of my life to a relationship, the few women I met during that period didn't find me available enough... but I didn't let it bother me because I was building up my career & still in my (late) 20s.

Of course something had to come along and challenge that balance I had going on. So my father got diagnosed with brain cancer & was losing mobility at an exponential rate in his last year of "life". My two brothers were 1) too busy being an aspergers case and 2) too busy being a drugged up loser to even realize how our father was suffering & losing his independence & autonomy. So my dad brings me on vacation as a caregiver, a week in cuba, his last time putting his feet in the ocean, our last time relaxing together... on our drive back from the airport he opens up.

He knows his days are numbered, he doesn't want to rott in a hospital being cared for by burnt out nurses, all he wants is to die in peace and not have to leave home until it's time to meet his maker. He asks me to move back in to take care of him & the family home. He's incredibly lonely by then, career psychologist now confined to the family house he built 30yrs before. After my first week of living with him, I realized it couldn't go on like that, the man who raised me, made sacrifices countless times to raise us the best he could after mom left, putting us first and always pushed things back to his retirement when it came to enjoying life was dying inside a frail shell of his former self. Now he was 59 and would never get to retire...

I had to take a decision & I did : I resigned from my teaching position, quit University & my 2nd job. I would put my life on hold until he left us, he deserved more than to die alone by himself after living his life helping others.

But it didn't take long, after a few weeks he had no strength left. One thursday afternoon in December I came back from running errands & found him semi-concious on the pee soaked couch. I picked him up, cleaned him, dressed him & called for an ambulance to come pick him up for his last drive through town.

Luckily I had been a volunteer for a palliative care center for years & made "the call" to the director of the place, within a day we had a bed in the most serene places available to die in. More painkillers Mr Rottie Sr. ? Here, have a double dose, call us back when it wears off.

Everything happened so quickly, he died the next Tuesday. Withing 4 days my life went from 5th gear to neutral... I was relieved he wasn't suffering anymore, but I was fucked up from all the stress I had been under. I waited until after the holidays to get back on the wagon & find a new job.

By then I was experiencing a new kind of loneliness, the one of losing the biggest & strongest pillar in my life as well as my best friends for the past few months, we had gotten so close. So of my friends were checking up on me here and there but I was left to myself, my two dysfunctional brothers were nowhere to be seen. Except the aspergers one who was executor of the will, he came by the family house to boss me around & eventually kick me out to sell it faster. That day I realized the only family I had were my fathers brother & sister, not my own. A new feeling of loneliness I hadn't felt before presented itself.

So not being the kind of guy to pout & drag his feet, I got a new job in a startup company. Lasted a year & they went belly up. I had given it all, thinking that dedicating myself to a new amazing job would help me get back on the horse, riding hard like I used to.

By then I was roommate with a long time friend (the one I used to help with her restaurant & caterings), she met a guy & decided to move out of the region. We had a huge fight because she was coming back on agreements we had shook on about our living arrangements, droping her life here for a guy she met 3 months before (it lasted a year & she was back in town).

By then I was sick of people, tired of assholes, dreamers & hypocrits, had too many knifes stuck in my back (yeah, I skipped over a few chapters) & the only person that used to give me guidance in periods like these was gone.

So my E.I. came in, having paid employment insurance for over 17yrs by then & never claiming any I decided to use it, fuck you all I'm on vacation ! My dads inheritance came in around that time (18 months later) so I bought a used camper trailer & moved to a private campgrounds owned by a friend of mine. Alone all week except weekends when others would come up to their campers. It was wonderful, 42 acres of land to relax on with my dog, never pressed to socialize with others unless I felt like it... I had a lot of healing to do, things to put in perspective & no more tolerance for people fucking with me. By end of august I was pretty much by myself (and now 2 doggos ! ), still living off of unemployment & inheritance money.

That time alone in the forest ( 8 months total ) was one of the best things in my life. I really had a chance to reassess my entire self... what did I want ? How bad did I want it ? Was it worth it ? Do I want a career or a job ? Who can I trust now ? Should I trust anyone ? What the fuck is their malfunction ? Why should I bother with people anymore ? Where's the happy guy always ready to help others gone too ? I miss that guy... is he dead inside me ? So much introspection to do, I was working at it everyday.

By October I was getting bored, I had to get back to work, but I was still deep in my anti-social depression... so I asked a high school friend who was now a struggling single mom of 2 if she'd rent me a room until I stabilized in my new job & got ready for my next chapter in life. It was wonderful, I got a forced return to social life with her & her 2 daughters, only once in the first month I drove up to my camper for a weekend & a break from the kids.

If it wouldn't have been for that opportunity to be alone by myself with a minimum of socializing every week, I don't think I would be out of my depression as much as I am today... I say this because I feel like once you hit that depression wall, it's always just around the corner if you're not careful. Loneliness can help you discover yourself, but it can also disconnect you from reality, its a double edge sword in so many ways. I couldn't bare to see my dad suffer alone by himself but suffering in my hole for a few months is what helped me the most.

A few things I learned through all this :

  • Be carefull with isolation, if you lose track of yourself it can be a daunting task to find yourself again...

  • Don't crash & burn in a basement, at least go outside & smell the god damn roses once in a while.

  • There's a whole world out there, explore it now, later will be too late because you might never make it.
